URRUTIA Punong Barangay Barangay Maysan, Valenzuela City Dear Sir: This has reference to your letter dated 08 July 2008, seeking advice on the inaction of the Appropriations Committee Chairman in the person of Kagawad Emilio Candido regarding the proposed Barangay Budget for the year 2008. You alleged that the said budget is deliberately not acted upon because of the following requests of Kagawad Candido, to wit: "Submission of appointment, plantiZZa at payroll ng mga kawani ng barangay sa nakaraang mga taon. Kopya ng 2006, 2007 annual at supplemental budget. Biodata ng ilang piling kawani gayun din ang mga bagong appoint at pagtanggaZ sa mga ito, na wata namang legal na basehan. PagtanggaZ sa aking mga kaanak sa barangay na nuon pang 1995 ay naglilingkod na sa tanggapang ito at sa aking pagkakaatam ay hindi naman ito isang career position. Financial statements at iba pang bagay na, ang COA ang may saklaw dito" These requests, according to you, have no basis in law as you specifically contended that under present conditions, the duties of the

iii -2- Appropriations Committee is limited on the following set of duties, which are as follows: "tiyakin kung napaglaanan ng tamang pondo ang lahat ng mandatory obligations katuZad ng 55% Personal Services, 10% SK Fund, 5% Gender & Development, 5% Calamity Fund, 2% Discretionary Fund at 20% Development Fund at MOOE na kailangan sa pagbuo ng budget". The proper resolution of this case before us hinges on the proper delineation of the duties and obligation of the Punong Barangay, on the one hand, and Sangguniang Barangay in the preparation and enactment or passage of the barangay annual budget, on the other. Sections 330 and 331 Of the Local Government Code provide, viz: "SEC. 330. Submission of Detailed Statements of Income and Expenditures for the Barangay Budgets.- On or before the fifteenth (15th) day of September of each year, the barangay treasurer shall submit to the punong barangay a statement covering the estimates of income and expenditures for the ensuing fiscal year, based on a certified statement issued by the city or municipal treasurer covering the estimates of income from Zocal sources for the barangay concerned. " "SEC. 331. Preparation of the Barangay Budget.- (a) Upon receipt of the statement of income and expenditures from the barangay treasurer, the punong barangay shall prepare the barangay budget for the ensuing fiscal year in the manner and within the period prescribed in this Titte and submit the annual barangay budget to the sangguniang barangay for legislative enactment. (b) The total annual appropriations for personal services of a barangay for one (I) fiscal year shall not exceed fifty-five percent (55%) of the total annual income actually realized from Zocal sources during the next preceding fiscal year. (c) The barangay shaZZ likewise be subject to the same budgetary requirements and limitations hereinabove prescribed.

There are two main phases in the life cycle of barangay budgets: preparatory phase and the legislative enactment phase. In the preparatory phase, the Punong Barangay essentially prepares the barangay budget based on the statement covering the estimates of income and expenditures submitted by the Barangay Treasurer on or before the 1 5th day of September. The Punong Barangay has until the 1 6ff of October to come up with the said budget proposal. In the preparation of said budget proposal, the Punong Barangay must comply with the limitation cited and set forth above and, pursuant to Section 324 (a) (b) (c) (d) of the Local Government Code, to wit: The "SEC. 324. Budgetary Requirements.- budgets of local government units for any fiscal year shall comply with the following requirements: (a) The aggregate amount appropriated shall not exceed the estimates of income; (b) Full provision shall be made for au statutory and contractual obligations Of the locat gotærnment unit concerned: Provided, however, That the amount of appropriations for debt servicing shall not exceed twenty percent (20%) of-Ute regular income of the Zocal government unit concerned; (c) In the case of provinces, cities, and municipalities, aid to component barangays shall be provided in amounts of not less than One Thousand Pesos (PI,OOO. 00) per barangay; and (d) Five (5%) percent Of the estimated revenue from regular sources shall be set aside as an annual lump sum appropriation for relief, reconstruction, rehabilitation or other works and services arising from the occurrence of calamities during the budget year: Provided, however, That such appropriation shatZ be used only in the area, or a portion thereof, of the local government unit or other areas declared by the Sanggunian concerned under a state of calamity." (as amended by RA 8185)

In its legislative enactment phase, the Sanggunian mainly enacts the ordinance or legislative authorization for the disbursement of barangay funds. Before the actual enactment, however, the proposed budget undergoes review and evaluation by the Appropriations Committee within the Sanggunian. While these duties are not so expressly provided under the Code, it is nonetheless vividly summarized in page 61 of the Updated Budget Operations Manual for Local Government Units issued by the Department of Budget and Management, to wit: "4.2 Role of the Committee on Appropriations. The Committee on Appropriations created as one of the standing committees within the Sanggunian, shall be responsible for conducting a preliminary review and evaluation of the executive budget. For the purpose, the committee may conduct its own budget hearing and may cau upon the Zocal finance committee, and heads of offices or departments. Thereafter, the committee shaZZ render its report, recommendation and draft Resolution and Ordinance to the sanggunian Such report, recommendation and draft proper. Resolution and Ordinance will then serzæ as the focus of deliberation. " It is further stated that "the sanggunian shaZZ ensure that the provision on budgetary requirements and generat limitations prescribed by Sections 324 and 331 are complied with in the proposed budget" (page 63, Ibid). Ergo, it 'is quite clear that the reasons relied upon by the Appropriations Committee Chairman on his alleged inaction on the proposed budget submitted by the Punong Barangay are outside the parameters enunciated in the abovestated rule of the DBM and thus, may be considered whimsical, capricious and without legal basis. In the meantime, so as not to hamper the operation and the delivery of basic services by the barangay, the Punong Barangay may resort to Section 23 of the Local Government Code, which provides: Failure to Enact the Annual "SEC. 323. Appropriations.- In case the sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations

at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shatt continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until ordinance gpprgyed, and other be taken up such sessions. If the sanggunian Stitt faits to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropr-iations of the preceding year shaZZ be deemed reenacted and shatt remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations for salaries and wages Of existing positions, statutory and contractual, obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budget' for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of fiznds shalt be in accordance therewith." (underlining ours) Hence, the Punong Barangay can properly disburse barangay funds based on the 2007 budget as a re-enacted budget. On the other hand, the Chairman of the Appropriations Committee and the other Members of the Sangguniang Barangay are hereby reminded of their mandated tasks under the said Section 323 Of the Code, which provides that in case the Sanggunian concerned failed to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. Compliance with the above Section 323 is clearly mandatory as can be gleaned from the use of the word "shall". Failure of the Sangguniang Barangay to comply therewith would make them vulnerable to a possible administrative case of dereliction of duty. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADE O Undersecretary Legal:09/La cc: The Regional Director DILG-NCR, LMP Bldg. Ermin Garcia Street, Cubao, Quezon City
